call_overview.title: About the call
call_overview.question: What does the call offer, and who can apply?

cards.title: What the call wants
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop, and which problem or need must it address?
cards.answer:
A commercial-scale plant in the Netherlands that produces e-SAF (synthetic aviation fuel made from renewable hydrogen and CO2), or the FEED study that prepares the investment decision for one.
The SDL (Tijdelijke subsidieregeling Stimulering Duurzame Luchtvaartbrandstoffen, a temporary Dutch subsidy scheme for sustainable aviation fuel) funds one of two project types per application:
- Preparation project (voorbereidingsproject): preparatory studies needed for an investment decision on an e-SAF plant, mainly a FEED study (Front-End Engineering and Design, the technical and process design work that underpins an investment decision), plus for example environmental studies, impact analyses and financial models.
- Realisation project (realisatieproject): building a new e-SAF plant, or extending, converting or adapting an existing industrial plant, including process installations, technical systems, supporting infrastructure, directly related engineering, testing and commissioning.
Excluded: building, extending or converting an electrolyser for hydrogen production, pilot projects, and the HEFA route (fuel from used cooking oil and fats).
The need comes from industry and national policy: e-SAF is four to six times as expensive as fossil kerosene and not yet proven at commercial scale, so investors hesitate, while the EU ReFuelEU Aviation regulation sets rising blending obligations for e-SAF. The plant must produce at least 51% e-SAF over its expected SAF output to fall under this round.

cards.title: Project impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
The plants must cut CO2 emissions from aviation by producing sustainable aviation fuel in the Netherlands at commercial scale, and make the country less dependent on imported and fossil fuels.
- Climate: the government indicates that about 167 kilotonnes of e-SAF a year would avoid about 0.52 million tonnes of CO2 a year at full operation; the national aim is 14% sustainable fuel in aviation by 2030 and only sustainable energy carriers by 2050.
- Production: a funded plant must stay in operation for 120 months after commissioning, and on average more than 80% of its output must be e-SAF; the rest may only be advanced bio-SAF or low-carbon fuels.
- Industry: the scheme aims to keep and transform skilled jobs in refining, chemicals and logistics, and to keep the Netherlands a European fuel production and distribution hub.
- Energy system: the government notes that projects may, where efficient, use imported intermediate products such as green methanol so as not to put unnecessary load on Dutch electricity and hydrogen demand.
- Knowledge: applicants must share non-confidential results, as first-of-a-kind plants are expected to bring learning effects and lower costs.

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer:
Companies that will develop, build and operate an e-SAF plant in the Netherlands; there is no consortium requirement.
- Lead applicant: a SAF-projectontwikkelaar (SAF project developer), defined as a company, or a partnership of several companies with legal personality, aimed at developing, building and operating a SAF production facility in the Netherlands. Several companies may apply together if they cooperate in one legal entity.
- Location: the applicant must have a permanent establishment or subsidiary in the Netherlands at the latest before the first advance payment, and may not be a company in difficulty.
- Partners and work: the project plan names the applicant and its essential subcontractors (uitbestedingsrelaties), with each party's role; one grant decision is issued per applicant per opening round.
- Suits best: refiners, chemical companies, fuel producers and project developers with a concrete e-SAF plant plan, together with their technology suppliers and engineering firms as subcontractors.

cards.title: Innovation
cards.question: How new must the project be, and in what must it innovate?
cards.answer:
No new technology is required: the scheme funds the first commercial-scale use of mature e-SAF production routes, not research or pilots.
The fuel must follow one of the production routes of ASTM D7566 (the international specification for synthetic jet fuel) and meet the EU Renewable Energy Directive's definition of renewable fuel of non-biological origin. Pilot projects, meant mainly to test and improve new technology, are rejected for realisation projects. The innovation lies in scaling up technology and plant design to commercial production, not in market arrangements or governance.

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The technology must be mature, at TRL 7–9 (from a prototype proven in an operational setting to a fully proven commercial system), and the realisation project ends with a plant in commercial operation.
cards.sources: Staatscourant 2026, 31133 (Tijdelijke subsidieregeling Stimulering Duurzame Luchtvaartbrandstoffen) · Toelichting § 2.1 Doel en reikwijdte; Artikel 13, eerste lid, onderdeel e

cards.title: Demonstration and integration of work
cards.question: Where must the solution be demonstrated, and how must the work fit with existing systems?
cards.answer:
The plant is not a demonstration but a commercial facility at a specific site in the Netherlands, which must operate for 120 months.
- Coherent system: a realisation project is defined as a coherent set of activities resulting in a production facility at a specific location, including technical installations, process units and supporting infrastructure that are functionally linked.
- Existing infrastructure: the applicant must show how it will source feedstocks such as methanol and sell the fuel, with letters of intent. The model project plan asks whether the grid operator can supply the electricity needed and whether the grid connection is secured, and names connection to the electricity grid, permits and final investment decision as critical milestones.
- Proof of operation: at the end, the applicant must show the plant was commissioned successfully, with its date, and works to the specified production volumes, for example with a Site Acceptance Test.

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer:
e-SAF plants are a new kind of large industrial electricity user, and this round decides which of them get built in the Netherlands, affecting future connection requests and congestion on TenneT's grid.
Our judgement: e-SAF is made from hydrogen produced with renewable electricity, and even though the round does not fund electrolysers, the plants and their hydrogen supply add major new demand. The regulation itself names grid congestion and late grid connections as one of two main risks for these projects, and the model project plan asks applicants whether their grid connection is secured. This links to TenneT's work on flexible, time-dependent connection contracts for large users and on how large new loads can act as flexible grid assets. TenneT could use the round's results to anticipate connection requests and could point developers to flexible connection options. TenneT cannot take part itself: only a SAF project developer that will build and operate the plant may apply, and the rules set out no role for a grid operator.

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
EUR 205,402,000 for e-SAF in this first round, shared by preparation and realisation projects; one application may take the whole amount.
- Total project size: not limited; with the maximum grant at the 45% base rate for realisation projects, the maximum grant corresponds to about EUR 456 million of eligible costs.
- Grant request: at most EUR 205,402,000 per application. A preparation project must request more than EUR 4 million; a request of EUR 4 million or less is rejected. Realisation projects have no minimum.
- Funding form: a project subsidy on actual eligible costs, with staff costs at a fixed rate of EUR 80 per hour.
A separate EUR 84,594,000 for advanced bio-SAF will open at a later, not yet announced date.

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
The rate depends on the project type and company size; the applicant must finance the rest itself.
- Preparation project, large company: at most 60% of eligible costs
- Preparation project, medium-sized company: at most 70%
- Preparation project, small company: at most 80%
- Realisation project, large company: at most 45% of eligible costs
- Realisation project, medium-sized company: at most 55%
- Realisation project, small company: at most 65%
- Co-financing conditions: aid may not be stacked on the same costs beyond the maximum aid intensity under the EU state aid rules (CEEAG for preparation, CISAF for realisation projects); certain national schemes cannot be combined, while EU funds managed centrally may be combined up to the maximum intensity.
- Evidence required: a financing plan that at least substantiates how the applicant's own share is financed, with recent annual accounts and, for external finance, signed agreements or letters of intent or term sheets.

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Only costs directly linked to the funded activities count, with staff at a fixed EUR 80 per hour.
- Eligible costs: for realisation projects, for example detailed engineering, land acquisition, purchase and installation of equipment, construction, testing and commissioning; for preparation projects, external services for the studies, environmental studies, impact analyses and financial modelling.
- Excluded costs: for preparation projects, costs made before the application and continuous or recurring activities, such as preparing permit applications, selecting suppliers and licensors, and work only for internal decision-making; regular operating costs are excluded for both types; costs of an electrolyser for hydrogen production are not eligible.

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
RVO pays 95% of the grant in advance, in four instalments linked to milestones, and the last 5% after the final account.
- Payment model: 15% within six weeks of the grant decision; then advances up to 65%, 85% and 95% of the grant in total as the applicant's three self-chosen milestones are reached; the final 5% at the final account (vaststelling). The minister may pay an advance in the year after a milestone if it is reached early.
- Financial reporting or audit: an auditor's report with the request for the final account; an annual progress report and a quarterly update of finances and planning.
- Recovery: the grant is reduced or reclaimed if the e-SAF share of output over 120 months falls below 80% (see the conditional requirements).

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: a complete application online at RVO, with eHerkenning level 3 (the Dutch business login), handled in order of receipt.
- Stage 1 — Application: 3 November 2026, 09:00, to 24 November 2026, 17:00; one application per production facility per period, for either a preparation or a realisation project, not both.
- Additional procedure: an incomplete application may be completed within the same period, but the date it becomes complete then counts as its date of receipt. If more complete applications arrive on one day than the budget allows, a lottery decides the order.
The minister may open up to five rounds over five years, only if enough budget remains; any next round starts on the first working day of November.
cards.sources:
Staatscourant 2026, 31133 (Tijdelijke subsidieregeling Stimulering Duurzame Luchtvaartbrandstoffen) · Artikel 5, vierde en vijfde lid; Artikel 6
Subsidieregeling Duurzame Luchtvaartbrandstoffen (SDL): e-SAF (RVO page) · Budget en aanvraagperiode; Voorwaarden; Aanvragen; Na uw aanvraag

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
Projects must start within six months of the grant decision; preparation projects must finish within 24 months, realisation projects for e-SAF have no maximum.
- Maximum duration: preparation project 24 months, extendable by the minister on request; realisation project for e-SAF not limited.
- Required start: the applicant may not have started the work or entered irreversible legal commitments before applying; permits and feasibility studies do not count as a start. The project must start within six months of the grant decision.
- Eligible-cost period: for preparation projects, costs made before the application are not eligible.
- Completion deadline: the request for the final account is due within 13 weeks of the project end date; after a realisation project, the plant must operate for 120 months.

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
RVO decides within at most 13 weeks of a complete application, by letter.
- Funding decision: within 13 weeks of receipt of the complete application.
- Conditions before starting: the decision is made subject to Parliament approving enough budget in the Infrastructure and Water Management budget; the applicant needs a permanent establishment or subsidiary in the Netherlands before the first advance.

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The online form plus a fixed set of annexes, all required at submission.
- Application form: the RVO online form; a project plan in the RVO model format, at most 30 pages excluding annexes, with a public summary of at most one A4.
- Budget: the RVO model budget with three self-chosen milestones, a target date and liquidity need for each, in line with the maximum advance per instalment.
- Mandatory annexes: a knowledge-dissemination plan; a financing plan for the applicant's own share; recent (consolidated) annual accounts no older than 18 months, including the group's; a declaration and decision chart showing the applicant is not a company in difficulty; the group's legal structure with shareholdings; a declaration of the SAF type.
- Realisation projects also: letters of intent for buying feedstocks such as methanol and selling the SAF, and a declaration that the fuel comes from renewable sources other than biomass and meets the sustainability and greenhouse gas criteria of article 29a of the Renewable Energy Directive.
- Registration: eHerkenning level 3.

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Applications are not ranked: RVO funds them in order of receipt, but rejects those that fail the scheme's quality tests.
- Evaluation criteria: rejection if there is not enough confidence in the project's quality (approach and method, risk management, feasibility, participating parties, efficient use of funds), if the knowledge-dissemination plan is of insufficient quality, if the project uses the HEFA route, if work has already started, or if the applicant is in difficulty. RVO also rejects an application if the subsidy has no incentive effect (the project would go ahead without it), and may reject it if technical or economic feasibility is not made plausible.
- Ranking rules: first come, first served; a lottery among the complete applications of the day the budget is oversubscribed.
- Budget assessment: RVO checks per activity and cost type whether costs are eligible before applying the rate.

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Realisation projects carry production obligations for ten years, with grant cuts if the plant produces too little e-SAF.
- Conditional — e-SAF share below 80%: if the average e-SAF share over 120 months is below 80%, or other fuels are produced, the grant is reduced by 1% to 100%, for example 5% at a 70–80% share and 100% below 30%.
- Conditional — annual reporting: each year for 120 months the recipient must report fuel volumes by type with an independent review.
- Conditional — hydrogen use: hydrogen used in production must cut greenhouse gas emissions by at least 70% compared with a fossil reference, shown in a separate calculation annex.
- Conditional — results sharing: on request, the recipient must help spread non-confidential results until five years after the final account, and must deliver a public report.
- Exception — e-SAF realisation projects: unlike advanced bio-SAF realisation projects, which must be ready within 48 months with grant cuts of 1% to 25% for delays, e-SAF realisation projects have no maximum duration and no delay penalty.
